_comment: Baseline of tests/engine-invariants.html. Each value hashes that configuration's rounded KPI set; open the harness and treat any changed fingerprint on an unchanged configuration as a regression. __all hashes the whole set.
_caveat: The hash covers the WHOLE KPI object, so ADDING an output key changes every fingerprint even though no number moved. A wholesale change across unrelated configurations usually means new KPI keys, not a regression. Confirm by extracting the previous engine (git show <prev>:src/calc.js), running both against the same inputs, and comparing only the keys that existed before. Re-baseline once that shows no drift.
_history: 860fe56 pre mixed-use. Mixed-use left all 34 fingerprints byte-identical. The debt-facility fix deliberately moved 29. Leasehold land added 5 KPI keys; a value-level diff confirmed zero freehold drift. Ground rent then moved to a monthly accrual, moving only the four leasehold fingerprints. Encumbered exit (leasehold NOI capitalised net of ground rent) added the annualRentAtExit key, re-hashing everything; a value-level diff over 300 numbers across 6 freehold configurations again confirmed zero drift, and leasehold exit values fell as intended. Ground rent was then found MISSING from totalCashCosts while present in grossCashflow - profit was overstated by the entire rent (83.2M vs 45.6M on a test scheme) while IRR was already correct, which is why it read as a high profit beside a modest return. Only the four leasehold fingerprints moved. Operating expenses then became a use so total uses equals total cost; no fingerprint moved.
_history2: The timeline was then re-cut to END on the last trading month: projectEndMonth switched from an exclusive to an inclusive convention, the three-month tail past the exit was dropped, and the exit moved from the month AFTER the hold onto its final month. Every fingerprint moves, because every horizon does - by four months (three of tail, one of boundary). A value-level diff against the previous engine confirmed the shape: revenue identical on all 48 configurations, and the only cost/profit movements are the four leasehold configurations, each falling by exactly one month of ground rent. Everything else that moved (IRR, NPV, payback, interest) follows from the shorter horizon and the earlier exit. Two consumers had latent off-by-ones that the tail had been absorbing: runWaterfall reads `horizon` as a month COUNT (new Array(horizon), slice(0, horizon), horizon - 1) so it needs lastMonth + 1, and the operating loop clamps opEnd against `horizon` as if it were a count when it is a last index. Both now fail loudly rather than silently, via the two new invariants.
